concepts.title: Meaning and Nature of Goodwill
concepts.description: Introduction to goodwill as an intangible asset representing the reputation and good name of a firm that enables it to earn higher profits than normal.
key_ideas: Definition of Goodwill as the value of reputation
Goodwill as an intangible but valuable asset
Distinction between tangible assets and goodwill
Role in earning super profits

concepts.title: Factors Affecting the Value of Goodwill
concepts.description: Analysis of the various internal and external factors that influence a firm's reputation and the monetary value of its goodwill.
key_ideas: Impact of favorable location on customer footfall
Efficiency of management and operational longevity
Nature of goods and market stability
Possession of patents, contracts, and trade advantages

concepts.title: Classification and Accounting Standard 26
concepts.description: Differentiation between Purchased and Self-generated Goodwill, and the rules prescribed by Accounting Standard 26 (Intangible Assets) regarding their recording in books.
key_ideas: Purchased Goodwill: Arises on acquisition, recorded in books
Self-generated Goodwill: Internally built, not recorded in books
AS-26 requirement: Asset recognition only when consideration is paid
Amortization of Purchased Goodwill

concepts.title: Need for Valuation of Goodwill
concepts.description: Identification of specific circumstances in a partnership where the valuation of goodwill becomes necessary to ensure fair treatment of partners.
key_ideas: Change in profit-sharing ratio among existing partners
Admission of a new partner
Retirement or death of a partner
Dissolution or amalgamation of the firm

concepts.title: Calculation of Adjusted Normal Profit
concepts.description: The process of normalizing past profits by adjusting for abnormal gains, abnormal losses, and non-recurring expenses to determine the true maintainable profit for valuation.
key_ideas: Deducting abnormal gains (e.g., sale of fixed assets)
Adding back abnormal losses (e.g., loss by fire)
Adjusting for non-business income (investments)
Rectifying accounting errors affecting past profits
